4B.4 The Law is to be taught and instructed privately and publicly.

points: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the Most High tells Jeremiah to take a roll of a book and write in it all the words He has spoken against Israel, against Judah, and against all the nations, from the days of Josiah until that day.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The purpose is that the house of Judah, hearing all the evil purposed against them, might return every man from his evil way so that He would forgive their iniquity and their sin.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Jeremiah calls Baruch the son of Neriah, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Most High upon the roll.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Because Jeremiah is shut up and cannot go into the house of the Most High, he sends Baruch to read the roll in the ears of the people on the fasting day, that they might present their supplication and turn from their evil way, for great is the anger and fury pronounced against this people.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Baruch does all that the prophet commanded, reading the book of the words of the Most High in the Most High's house.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: In the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, a fast is proclaimed before the Most High to all the people in Jerusalem and those who came from the cities of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Baruch reads the words of Jeremiah in the temple in the chamber of Gemariah, in the ears of all the people.

Michaiah the son of Gemariah, having heard the words, goes down into the king's house to the scribe's chamber where all the princes are sitting, and declares to them all he had heard when Baruch read.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The princes send Jehudi to bring Baruch with the roll, and they ask him to sit and read it in their ears.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: When they hear all the words they are afraid, both one and another, and say they will surely tell the king; they ask Baruch how he wrote all these words, and he answers that Jeremiah pronounced them with his mouth while Baruch wrote them with ink in the book.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The princes tell Baruch to go hide himself and Jeremiah, and to let no man know where they are.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The princes lay up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe and tell all the words in the ears of the king, who sends Jehudi to fetch it and read it before him and the princes.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The king sits in the winter house in the ninth month with a fire burning on the hearth; as Jehudi reads three or four leaves, the king cuts them with a penknife and casts them into the fire until the whole roll is consumed.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Neither the king nor his servants are afraid nor rend their garments; though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah make intercession that he not burn the roll, he will not hear, and he commands that Baruch and Jeremiah be seized, but the Most High hides them.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: After the king burns the roll, the word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah to take another roll and write all the former words that Jehoiakim had burned.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Against Jehoiakim He pronounces that he shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night, and He will punish him, his seed, and his servants for their iniquity.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Jeremiah gives a second roll to Baruch, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the burned book, and many like words are added besides.
